did_you_know.text: Psalm 86 opens with the title “A Prayer of David,” and the speaker describes himself as “poor and needy”—an expression of distress and complete dependence on the LORD.
From the very beginning of the psalm, requests for protection, salvation, and trust in the LORD appear together: “Guard my life,” “Save Your servant,” and “who trusts in You.”
The speaker describes his prayer as ongoing, not a one-time request: “For to You I call all day long.”
This verse presents the LORD as good, forgiving, and abundant in kindness, and extends the request beyond the speaker himself—to “all who call on You.”
The psalmist emphasizes the LORD’s uniqueness with two parallel statements: “There is none like You among the gods” and “there are no deeds like Yours.”
According to the psalm’s vision, all the nations the LORD has made will come before Him, bow down, and honor His name; this highlights the universal recognition of His kingship.
The request “Unite my heart to fear Your name” expresses the desire for an undivided heart, focused on reverence for the LORD rather than divided or hesitant worship.

The psalm contrasts the “arrogant” and “ruthless” people who seek the speaker’s life with the LORD, who is described as compassionate, gracious, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness and faithfulness.

The expression “son of Your maidservant” appears alongside the request “Give Your strength to Your servant,” highlighting the connection between belonging, service, and the request for strength and deliverance.
At the end, the psalmist asks for “a sign of Your favor”—a visible sign of the LORD’s kindness that will allow his enemies to see that the LORD has helped and comforted him.
